title: Lovable
summary: A natural-language web-app workflow to evaluate with an explicit handoff plan.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: Project code can be synchronized with Git providers; database and service migration still need a separate plan.

facts.label: Usage basis
facts.value: Credits cover build and runtime usage categories; inspect the workspace usage breakdown.

prices.name: Pro — annual commitment
prices.billing: Annual total, not a monthly charge

sections.heading: Prototype a real boundary
paragraphs: Start with one persisted entity, one signed-in interaction and one invalid input. Inspect what happens when the user is not authorized. A polished interface should not substitute for a test of permissions and data validation.

sections.heading: Plan the handoff
paragraphs: Use the documented ownership and hosting guidance to inventory what moves with the code and what needs separate operations. Confirm which application framework your project uses before choosing a deployment target. Database and secret migration deserve their own rehearsal.

pros.text: Lovable documents natural-language app building with project code that can sync to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket.
Workspaces support shared projects and a shared credit pool for team members.

cons.text: Usage is credit-based across product activities, and actual consumption depends on the feature and work performed.
Git synchronization covers the codebase; separately validate database, hosting and secret migration for the complete application.

faqs.question: Can a Lovable project join an existing Git workflow?
faqs.answer: The documentation says project code can sync to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. Confirm the target repository workflow and separately rehearse moving runtime services.

faqs.question: Can I estimate one fixed credit cost per feature?
faqs.answer: No universal conversion is documented. Review workspace usage and test the actual workflow because credit consumption varies by feature and activity.

verdict: Shortlist Lovable for a web prototype whose code and deployment ownership you can review before launch. Budget iteration and ongoing operation separately.
notFor: Teams treating generated output as production-ready without security review
migration: Before committing, rehearse code handoff, database export and secret replacement. Moving code alone does not prove the complete service can be operated elsewhere.
